title: H2 precedence / combined H2+H3 interpretation
status: registered before any T-E4 or T-E4K1 matrix data exists
authority: The project owner's decision, taken while the experiment was still blind to treatment (no T-E4 or T-E4K1 matrix cell had run), on the observation recorded with pre-registration v2 that "¬H1 ∧ H3" can still apply beside "H2". The issue, the four rules and the reported statement are the owner's text verbatim; only emphasis and code formatting are removed, and the rules are numbered in the owner's order.
preservation: Pre-registrations v1 and v2 and analysis freezes v1 and v2 are preserved permanently, byte for byte. Nothing in them is edited. Pre-registration v3 is pre-registration v2 together with this amendment.

finding.evidence: The registered definitions only; no data.
finding.text: When "¬H1 ∧ H3" and "H2" apply together, the v1 and v2 readings report both rows, and their conclusions point to different next steps.

issue: The issue is not that H2 ∧ ¬H1 ∧ H3 is ambiguous. It actually gives useful discrimination. The problem is that the old ¬H1 ∧ H3 interpretation says, in effect, the in-tick order line closes and the residual is the opening-pass effect. That statement is too broad if H2 is simultaneously supported, because H2 says the multi-pass privilege does follow the final pre-sample position. We shouldn't allow both conclusions to stand side by side.

rules.text: If H2 is SUPPORTED, the H2 interpretation takes precedence over the standalone ¬H1 ∧ H3 interpretation.

If H2 and H3 are both SUPPORTED, report: “The treatment identifies two contest-class-specific signatures. In MULTI-PASS matchups, the privilege follows the final pre-sample chunk, supporting an evaluation-adjacency/final-position mechanism. In OPENING-ONLY matchups, last-side persistence remains, consistent with an opening-pass mechanism. H3 does not override H2 and does not close the in-tick order line globally. Evaluation structure is the registered next question for the MULTI-PASS effect; anchor/core-0 co-location remains a separate follow-up for the OPENING-ONLY residual.”
Do not additionally emit the old standalone ¬H1 ∧ H3 conclusion.
No hypotheses, thresholds, populations, metrics, matrix, treatment semantics, or analyzer measurements change.

reading.text: O-INTERPRETATION-2 (and through it O-INTERPRETATION) is applied first, unchanged, and its result is reported as the v2 reading. O-INTERPRETATION-3 then acts on that reading, reading statuses as O-INTERPRETATION does. Precedence (rules 1 and 3): when E4-H2 is SUPPORTED and the row "¬H1 ∧ H3" is still in the reading, that row is withheld and "H2" stands. Combined outcome (rule 2): when E4-H2 and E4-H3 are both SUPPORTED, the combined outcome "H2 ∧ H3" is reported immediately after "H2". The "H2" row is kept, because it is the H2 interpretation that takes precedence and the combined statement restates and extends it; the amendment removes only the standalone "¬H1 ∧ H3" conclusion. Whenever E4-H2 is SUPPORTED the "H2" row applies, so the combined outcome always follows it. Everything else in the v2 reading is unchanged: O-INTERPRETATION-2's rules 1 and 3 and its H3 note, every other row, the pathology row (H5, H6, H8) and a D9′ STOP. After O-INTERPRETATION-3 the standalone "¬H1 ∧ H3" conclusion is never reported: with E4-H0 SUPPORTED, O-INTERPRETATION-2 rule 1 withholds it; with E4-H0 REFUTED and no other main row, O-INTERPRETATION-2 rule 3 replaces it; and the only other main row that can apply beside it, since it requires E4-H1 REFUTED, is "H2", where it is withheld here. The label "H2 ∧ H3" names a reading outcome, not a new hypothesis or criterion.

outcome.conclusion: The treatment identifies two contest-class-specific signatures. In MULTI-PASS matchups, the privilege follows the final pre-sample chunk, supporting an evaluation-adjacency/final-position mechanism. In OPENING-ONLY matchups, last-side persistence remains, consistent with an opening-pass mechanism. H3 does not override H2 and does not close the in-tick order line globally. Evaluation structure is the registered next question for the MULTI-PASS effect; anchor/core-0 co-location remains a separate follow-up for the OPENING-ONLY residual.
